title: EDiR Practice Set 1 · emergency and general radiology
subtitle: Radform original · abbreviated EDiR-style practice · English
disclaimer: Simulacro original de Radform basado en la estructura publicada del EDiR. No contiene preguntas oficiales ni bancos de pago.

questions.question: Which CT findings support acute appendicitis? Choose all that apply.
options: Periappendiceal inflammation must always be absent
questions.explanation: Appendiceal enlargement and surrounding inflammatory change are typical; an appendicolith may be present.

questions.question: Which findings may occur in cardiogenic pulmonary oedema? Choose all that apply.
questions.explanation: Cardiomegaly, interstitial/alveolar oedema and pleural effusions may coexist.

questions.question: Marked diffusion restriction with low ADC is most typical of:
questions.explanation: Acute cytotoxic oedema characteristically restricts diffusion.

questions.question: Which feature of a solid renal mass increases concern for renal cell carcinoma?
options: Macroscopic fat typical of a classic angiomyolipoma
Pure water attenuation with no enhancement
questions.explanation: Enhancement confirms vascularised solid tissue and raises concern for neoplasm.

questions.question: Which mammographic findings warrant further assessment? Choose all that apply.
options: A stable axillary node with a preserved fatty hilum as the only finding
questions.explanation: Suspicious calcification morphology, distortion and a spiculated mass require diagnostic work-up.

questions.question: STIR imaging is particularly useful for:
options: Suppressing fat and increasing conspicuity of oedema
Measuring bone mineral density on CT
questions.explanation: STIR suppresses fat signal and highlights fluid-rich abnormalities such as oedema.

questions.question: The direct CT pulmonary angiography sign of acute pulmonary embolism is:
options: An intraluminal pulmonary arterial filling defect
questions.explanation: Acute thrombus appears as a filling defect within an opacified pulmonary artery.

questions.question: Which measures reduce radiation dose in paediatric CT? Choose all that apply.
options: Repeat multiphase acquisitions without clinical indication
questions.explanation: Patient-size adaptation, limiting coverage and modern reconstruction reduce unnecessary dose.

cases.title: Right upper quadrant pain
cases.stem: A patient presents with fever and right upper quadrant pain. Ultrasound demonstrates gallstones, gallbladder wall thickening and pericholecystic fluid.

questions.question: What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The combination of gallstones, wall thickening and inflammatory change is typical of acute cholecystitis.

questions.question: Which additional ultrasound finding would further support the diagnosis?
questions.explanation: A focal sonographic Murphy sign is a useful supportive feature in the appropriate clinical setting.

cases.title: Acute pleuritic chest pain
cases.stem: A young adult presents with sudden pleuritic chest pain and dyspnoea. Chest radiography is performed.

questions.question: A visible visceral pleural line with absent peripheral lung markings indicates:
questions.explanation: A pleural line with no lung markings peripheral to it is the classic radiographic appearance of pneumothorax.

questions.question: Which radiographic feature would raise concern for tension physiology?
options: Mediastinal shift away from a large pneumothorax in the appropriate clinical context
questions.explanation: A large pneumothorax with contralateral mediastinal displacement may indicate tension physiology and requires urgent clinical action.

cases.title: Acute aortic syndrome
cases.stem: A 64-year-old man presents with sudden severe chest pain radiating to the back. CTA of the aorta is performed.

questions.question: An intimal flap separating true and false lumina indicates:
questions.explanation: An intimal flap defining two channels is diagnostic of aortic dissection.

questions.question: If the ascending aorta is involved, the Stanford classification is:
questions.explanation: Any dissection involving the ascending aorta is Stanford type A.

questions.question: Which response would be potentially unsafe?
options: Urgently communicate a Stanford type A dissection
Describe the finding as incidental and clinically insignificant
questions.explanation: Failure to recognise and communicate a type A dissection may have catastrophic consequences.

cases.title: Acute focal neurological deficit
cases.stem: A 72-year-old woman presents 80 minutes after onset of aphasia and right-sided weakness.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of the initial non-contrast CT?
options: Exclude intracranial haemorrhage and assess early ischaemic change
questions.explanation: Non-contrast CT rapidly excludes haemorrhage and provides information on early ischaemic change.

questions.question: A left M1 occlusion on CTA would be concordant with:
options: Isolated left leg weakness from a spinal lesion
questions.explanation: A dominant left middle cerebral artery occlusion can cause aphasia and contralateral motor deficit.

questions.question: Which radiology action would be potentially unsafe?
options: Rapidly communicating a proximal large-vessel occlusion
Deliberately delaying the report for several hours despite a treatment window
Integrating non-contrast CT and CTA findings
questions.explanation: Avoidable delay can remove access to time-dependent reperfusion therapy.
